pronunciation_note: Say a soft hiss /s/ after sounds like p, t, k, f (cats); say a soft buzz /z/ after most other sounds, including vowels (dogs, runs).
mnemonic: Ess the Seed-Pip lands on the end of a word to show there's more than one, or that it's happening right now — listen for his soft hiss or buzz.

character.name: Ess the Seed-Pip
character.blurb: A tiny seed-pip who hops onto the end of words, landing so softly he only ever adds a hiss or a buzz, never a whole new word.

formation_cue: Add '-s' straight onto most root words with no change (cat→cats). If the word already ends in a hissing or buzzing letter string — s, x, sh, ch or ss — use '-es' instead.
action: Wiggle one finger, then suddenly flash all five, to show 'one becomes many'.

pronunciation_note: Say it as a whole extra syllable, 'iz', so the word gets one more beat you can clap — box becomes two claps: box-es.
mnemonic: Ezra the Bee always adds his own buzzing beat — '-es' — onto words that already end in a hiss, like box or bus.

character.name: Ezra the Bee
character.blurb: A busy bee who buzzes in with an extra beat whenever a word already ends in a hiss, so we can hear the ending properly.

formation_cue: Add '-es' (not just '-s') when the root word ends in s, ss, x, ch or sh — it makes a whole new beat you can hear and clap: box→boxes, bus→buses, dish→dishes.
action: Cup a hand behind your ear and add a little extra nod, as if catching the extra beat.

pronunciation_note: Say the 'ng' sound through your nose at the end, like the middle of 'sing' — don't say 'in' or 'een'.
mnemonic: Inga the Butterfly is always mid-flutter — add '-ing' to show an action is happening this very moment.

character.name: Inga the Butterfly
character.blurb: A butterfly who never sits still — she's always mid-flutter, which is why she loves showing off actions happening right now.

formation_cue: Add '-ing' straight on for most words (jump→jumping). Drop a silent 'e' first (make→making). Double a short-vowel-plus-consonant ending first (run→running).
action: Jog on the spot with arms pumping, to show the action happening right now.

pronunciation_note: It can sound like /t/ (jumped), /d/ (played), or a whole extra beat /ɪd/ (wanted) — listen to the sound the root word ends in to know which.
mnemonic: Eddy the Snail leaves his trail behind him — add '-ed' to show something already happened.

character.name: Eddy the Snail
character.blurb: A slow, thoughtful snail who always leaves a shiny trail behind him, showing where he has already been.

formation_cue: Add '-ed' straight on for most words (jump→jumped). Drop a silent 'e' first (like→liked). Double a short-vowel-plus-consonant ending first (stop→stopped). A few words change completely instead (go→went) — these are learned separately as tricky past tenses.
action: Point back over your shoulder with your thumb, to show the action is already behind you.

pronunciation_note: Say a short, clear 'un' — the stress usually stays on the main word behind it, not on 'un-' itself.
mnemonic: Una the Owl perches right at the front of a word and turns its meaning the opposite way round.

character.name: Una the Owl
character.blurb: A wise owl who can turn her head almost all the way round, always ready to flip things the opposite way.

formation_cue: Add 'un-' to the very front of a whole word, with no changes to the root word underneath it: happy→unhappy, do→undo, pack→unpack.
action: Cross both arms into an X in front of your chest, then snap them open, to show 'the opposite'.

pronunciation_note: Say a short, clear 'dis' with a soft hiss on the end — the stress usually stays on the main word behind it.
mnemonic: Diz the Hedgehog sits at the front of a word and curls it up into its opposite.

character.name: Diz the Hedgehog
character.blurb: A small, prickly hedgehog who curls into a tight ball whenever he wants to say 'no thank you, not that'.

formation_cue: Add 'dis-' to the very front of a whole word, with no changes to the root word underneath it: agree→disagree, appear→disappear, like→dislike.
action: Curl into a small ball on the floor, then slowly uncurl while shaking your head 'no'.

pronunciation_note: Say a soft, relaxed 'uh' sound at the end — in most British accents you won't hear a strong 'r'.
mnemonic: Erno the Acorn loves comparing — add '-er' to say one thing is more than another, or to name someone who does something.

character.name: Erno the Acorn
character.blurb: A proud little acorn who's always comparing himself to the acorn next to him, hoping to grow just a bit bigger.

formation_cue: Add '-er' straight on for most words (fast→faster). Drop a silent 'e' first (large→larger). Double a short-vowel-plus-consonant ending first (big→bigger). To mean 'a person who does this', add '-er' to an action word (run→runner).
action: Stand on tiptoes and stretch one hand a little higher than the other.

pronunciation_note: Say a clear extra beat, 'ist', at the end — it always adds a whole new syllable you can clap.
mnemonic: Essie the Sunflower stretches up taller than all the rest — add '-est' when something is the most, out of everyone.

character.name: Essie the Sunflower
character.blurb: A sunflower who stretches taller than every other flower in the patch, always reaching to be the very best.

formation_cue: Add '-est' straight on for most words (fast→fastest). Drop a silent 'e' first (large→largest). Double a short-vowel-plus-consonant ending first (big→biggest).
action: Stand on tiptoes and stretch both hands as high as they'll go, higher than everyone else.
